findings.claim: Nothing on the verilator_bin thread-pool or exit path changed between v5.050 and v5.052, so the upstream 4931 exit race should behave exactly as it does in v5.050.
findings.evidence: `git diff --quiet v5.050 v5.052 -- src/V3ThreadPool.cpp src/V3ThreadPool.h src/V3Mutex.h` reports no diff. In src/Verilator.cpp the only diff hunks are in process() (adds V3AssertCommon::lowerSequenceEvents; drops evalp(nullptr)/evalNbap(nullptr)) and in the selfTest list (drops V3ScoreboardBase/V3Order::selfTestParallel). The thread-pool setup at v5.052 src/Verilator.cpp:720 `v3Global.threadPoolp(new V3ThreadPool{v3Global.opt.verilateJobs()});` and the shutdown at :926 `v3Global.shutdown();` are unchanged, and the V3Global diff has no shutdown/vlExit/thread lines. The Changes file has no thread-pool entry.
findings.impact: Same exit behaviour as v5.050. Keeping '--build-jobs 0 --verilate-jobs 1' still means verilator_bin runs a 1-thread pool.
findings.expected_measurement: The '-j 0' exit-abort rate should be statistically the same as in the v5.050 row, and '--build-jobs 0 --verilate-jobs 1' should still give 0 aborts in 3000 runs.

findings.claim: -j, --build-jobs and --verilate-jobs keep the same meaning and defaults (0 means VlOs::getProcessDefaultParallelism()), so svsim's flags are still valid.
findings.evidence: The v5.050..v5.052 diff of src/V3Options.cpp touches only -assert-unroll-limit, -fdfg-break-cycles and the TSAN getSupported/showVersion code. At v5.052, src/V3Options.cpp:1325 `DECL_OPTION("-build-jobs" ... } else if (val == 0) { val = VlOs::getProcessDefaultParallelism();` and :1885 `DECL_OPTION("-verilate-jobs" ...` are identical to v5.050. bin/verilator only gains a doc line for `+verilator+assert+lock`. src/V3EmitMk.cpp changes are cosmetic (puts becomes putSet).
findings.impact: No change to how svsim invokes Verilator.
findings.expected_measurement: The svsim command line is accepted unchanged. Generated Makefiles still run make with -j<nproc> for '--build-jobs 0'.

findings.claim: The $urandom/$random RNG and +verilator+seed+ handling did not change in this range, so v5.052 should give the same numbers as v5.050. With no seed, output is identical on every run and equals the +verilator+seed+1 output, because the default seed is 1. +verilator+seed+0 is accepted and picks a random seed. Seed-1 output differs from 5.020's.
findings.evidence: The v5.050..v5.052 diff of include/verilated.cpp has no hunk in VlRNG::VlRNG / vl_thread_rng / vl_rng_state_from_seed (v5.052 verilated.cpp:444-548), in commandArgVl seed parsing (:3621-3629, `if (u64 == 0) u64 = pickRandomSeed(); randSeed(static_cast<int>(u64));`) or in randSeedDefault64 (:3703). verilated.h:528 `int m_randSeed = 1;  // Random seed (default 1; +verilator+seed+0 picks at parse time)`. vl_thread_rng seeds through `vl_rng_state_from_seed(...randSeedDefault64())` (splitmix64), whereas 5.020 used `t_rng.m_state[0] = ...randSeedDefault64(); t_rng.m_state[1] = t_rng.m_state[0];` (scratchpad verilated_5020.cpp:356-361). Both differences from 5.020 date from before v5.050: c1e343d9 (#6956) and 0e423a4b 'Fix `+verilator+seed` to default to 1, and 0 to randomly select (#7325) (#7516)'.
findings.impact: Runs stay deterministic without a seed. RANDOMIZE_REG_INIT/MEM_INIT values per seed match v5.050 but not 5.020, so cycle-exact results that depend on random initial state may differ from 5.020.
findings.expected_measurement: Same as the v5.050 row: no-seed output identical across runs and equal to the seed-1 output. Seed-1 is not 8084023f f77f7fff ff7fffff fffffffc (the 5.020 values). +verilator+seed+0 is accepted, and the run is not rejected.

findings.claim: The 'Optimize random initialization' rewrite gives the same values as before: it reads the thread context once per variable instead of once per word. It also removes the unused VL_RAND_RESET_Q and VL_RAND_RESET_W from the runtime header.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Optimize random initialization. [Geza Lore, Testorrent USA, Inc.]'. Commit 1106e89c rewrites include/verilated.cpp VL_SCOPED_RAND_RESET_{I,Q,W} and VL_RAND_RESET_I. For randReset 0 the result is zeros (VL_MEMSET_ZERO_W); for 1 it is ones (VL_MEMSET_ONES_W); for 2 it is the same `VlRNG rng{randSeed() ^ scopeHash ^ salt}` sequence. It deletes `extern QData VL_RAND_RESET_Q` and `extern WDataOutP VL_RAND_RESET_W` from include/verilated_funcs.h.
findings.impact: x-initial values are unchanged (default +verilator+rand+reset+ is 0, so zeros). The svsim driver does not reference the removed functions.
findings.expected_measurement: Initial values and $urandom sequences are the same as v5.050. Model construction may be slightly faster.

findings.claim: Seed arguments of $random(seed) and dist functions are now treated as read-write instead of write-only. This only matters when a seed variable is passed.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Fix R/W references to random builtin function seeds (#8112).' Commit 621a67e8, src/V3LinkLValue.cpp: `if (!nodep->urandom()) m_setRefLvalue = VAccess::READWRITE;` (was WRITE), and the same for AstNodeDistBiop/Triop.
findings.impact: None. The project defines RANDOM as $urandom with no seed argument.
findings.expected_measurement: n/a

findings.claim: The scheduling eval loop moved out of generated code into the runtime class VerilatedEvalLoop, and VerilatedModel gained pure-virtual entry points. The public model API that svsim uses is unchanged, and the order 'static -> initial -> settle, then set didInit' is the same, so svsim's re-entrant eval should still work.
findings.evidence: Commit 8546d5db 'Internals: Move the eval loop into the runtime library (#8225)': "The model's 'eval' and 'eval_step' remain the top level entry points, and are backward compatible." v5.052 include/verilated.cpp:4055 evalImpl calls evalStatic/evalInitial(:4072)/Stl loop and then `m_model.m_didInit = true;` (:4078). v5.050 src/V3EmitCModel.cpp:423 also set `__Vm_didInit = true` after _eval_settle. V3EmitCModel.cpp:190-216 still emits eval(), eval_step(), final(), eventsPending() and nextTimeSlot(). The driver uses only those plus VerilatedContext (simulation-driver.cpp:999-1060). Its re-entrant testbench->eval() comes from `always @(simulationState)` -> simulation_body, which runs after init.
findings.impact: No source change should be needed in svsim. The C++ uses only C++17 constructs (VL_CONSTEXPR_CXX17).
findings.expected_measurement: All 53 ChiselSim builds compile with -std=c++17 and the tests pass with the same cycle counts as v5.050.

findings.claim: --assert-unroll-limit is now deprecated and has no effect; passing it emits a DEPRECATED warning. svsim does not pass it.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Remove and deprecate `--assert-unroll-limit`. (#8096).' v5.052 src/V3Options.cpp:1306-1307 `DECL_OPTION("-assert-unroll-limit", CbVal, [fl](const char*) { fl->v3warn(DEPRECATED, "Option '--assert-unroll-limit' is deprecated and has no effect.");`. In the same file (:1481), -fdfg-break-cycles is deprecated as well.
findings.impact: None for svsim's option set (--cc --exe --build -o --top-module --Mdir --assert --timescale -CFLAGS +define -F are all still declared).
findings.expected_measurement: No DEPRECATED warning in the builds.

findings.claim: The new MULTIDRIVENPROC warning (a whole variable driven by more than one plain always block) is a style warning and is off by default.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Add MULTIDRIVENPROC warning for signals driven by multiple plain always blocks (#7968).' v5.052 src/V3Error.h:300-305 styleError() includes `m_e == MULTIDRIVENPROC`, and defaultsOff() covers styleError(). docs/guide/warnings.rst: 'Disabled by default as this is a code-style warning'.
findings.impact: No new warnings without -Wall. svsim does not pass -Wall.
findings.expected_measurement: Still 0 %Warning across the 53 builds.

findings.claim: The new SIMILARNAME warning (names that differ only in case) is a style warning and is off by default.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Add SIMILARNAME warning when variables have names that differ in case (#7992) (#8020) (#8186) (#8226) (#8233).' v5.052 src/V3Error.h:305 `m_e == SIMILARNAME` is in styleError(). It is emitted from src/V3LinkDot.cpp:367.
findings.impact: Firtool names like io_a/io_A would only warn under -Wall or -Wstyle.
findings.expected_measurement: Still 0 %Warning.

findings.claim: NEVERMATCH is on by default but is emitted only for SVA intersect/within sequences that statically can never match.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Add NEVERMATCH warning when an SVA sequence can never match (#8176) (#8183).' Its only emitter is v5.052 src/V3AssertNfa.cpp:1267 in buildNeverMatchIntersect ('Empty common-length intersection').
findings.impact: Firtool's Chisel assertions do not use intersect/within, so no effect is expected.
findings.expected_measurement: Still 0 %Warning.

findings.claim: MULTIDRIVEN, which is on by default, now also fires when a clocking-block output conflicts with another driver. New errors were added for static virtual functions and for scalars passed to array task arguments. None of these constructs appear in Chisel/firtool output.
findings.evidence: Commit 29fd2cf9 'Add MULTIDRIVEN checks for clocking block outputs (#7987)' (src/V3Undriven.cpp warnClockingDriven). Changes: '* Add error on static virtual functions (#7932).' and '* Add error when scalar is passed to array task argument (#7948).'
findings.impact: None expected. Firtool emits no clocking blocks, classes or array task arguments.
findings.expected_measurement: Still 0 %Warning or %Error.

findings.claim: V3Gate no longer inlines non-constant values assigned in `initial` logic into their use sites; they are now treated like static initializers. This fixes a miscompile for variables that are assigned only in initial blocks.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Fix initial statements with gate optimization (#8250). [Prithayan Barua]'. Commit 3c121c0a, src/V3Gate.cpp:228-230 `} else if (m_inStaticActive || m_inInitialActive) { // Runs only once, so its output must not be treated as live combinational logic m_logicVertexp->setStaticInit();`. At :588, `if (lVtxp->staticInit()) return false;` blocks inlining.
findings.impact: Relevant to firtool RANDOMIZE_* initial blocks, but registers also have always-block drivers and _RANDOM is an unpacked array, which was already not inlined. A behaviour change is unlikely but possible for initial-only variables.
findings.expected_measurement: Most likely identical results and cycles to v5.050. Any difference would show up only with RANDOMIZE_REG_INIT/MEM_INIT enabled.

findings.claim: The fix for $finish continuing the event loop only stops user named-event (`->ev`/`@ev`) triggers after $finish or while a $finish is pending.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Fix $finish continuing event loop (#7267) (#7950).' Commit b70696fc changes only the EVENT_IS_FIRED trigger in src/V3SenExprBuilder.h (v5.052 :290-304): `VL_LIKELY(!vlSymsp->_vm_contextp__->gotFinish() && !vlSymsp->_vm_contextp__->finishPending())`, plus the finishPending counter in VL_FINISH_MT.
findings.impact: None. Firtool RTL and the svsim testbench (`always @(simulationState)`) use no named events. svsim still detects $finish through context->gotFinish().
findings.expected_measurement: Same pass/fail and cycle counts as v5.050.

findings.claim: The reordering of queued $finish/$stop/$fatal requests only matters when they are posted from mtask worker threads. In a single-threaded model the request still runs immediately.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Fix queued $finish/$stop request thread ordering (#7946 prep) (#7952).' Commit 925a6640 adds stopRequestReserve/finishPendingInc around VerilatedThreadMsgQueue::post in include/verilated.cpp:245-272. In v5.052 include/verilated_imp.h:161-163, `if (Verilated::mtaskId() == 0) { msg.run(); }` runs the request immediately.
findings.impact: None for svsim, which does not use --threads. Chisel assertion $fatal and stop $finish behave as before.
findings.expected_measurement: Assertion-failure tests fail the same way as in v5.050.

findings.claim: User-written sampled-value functions ($past and the $rose/$fell/$stable/$changed family) now return the expression's default sampled value before enough clock ticks have elapsed. Verilator's internal property-lowering history is not affected.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Fix sampled-value functions output on the first cycle (#8162).' Commit 7f933372, src/V3Assert.cpp: new DefaultSampledValueVisitor and `// Before enough clock ticks, $past returns the expression's default sampled value.` with an AstInitialStatic on the _Vpast_ vars, plus the comment 'Source sampled-value history is initialized, unlike internal property-lowering history.'
findings.impact: This only matters if the RTL uses $past-style functions, for example via chisel3.ltl. Plain Chisel assert/printf are not affected.
findings.expected_measurement: No change unless such functions are used, in which case only first-cycle assertion outcomes could differ.

findings.claim: `disable iff` is now applied in the NFA lowering of multi-cycle SVA even when a snapshot variable exists. This changes pass/fail counts for multi-cycle properties when the disable condition pulses mid-window.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Fix mid-window disable iff (#7792) (#7869).' Commit ec124a09, src/V3AssertNfa.cpp: `if (c.disableExprp && !c.snapshotVarp)` becomes `if (c.disableExprp)` in three places. In test t_prop_always.v the expected count goes from `disable_bounded_fail_q.size(), 13` to `8`.
findings.impact: This only matters for multi-cycle sequences/properties with `disable iff`. Single-cycle Chisel assertions are not affected.
findings.expected_measurement: No change for single-cycle assertions.

findings.claim: DFG peephole rewrites no longer turn a guarded out-of-bounds array read (cond ? arr[i] : x) into an unguarded and/or expression. This fixes a possible crash or garbage read in v5.050.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Fix DFG misoptimizing bound checks (#7755).' Commit 853ee5df, src/V3DfgPeephole.cpp adds `|| vtxp->rhsp()->unsafe()` and `&& !elsep->unsafe()` guards to the LogAnd/LogOr/Cond rewrites (REPLACE_COND_WITH_THEN_BRANCH_ZERO etc.). Test t_dfg_oob_array_access.v.
findings.impact: This could matter for firtool code that reads Vec/Mem with a dynamic index under a guard. It only changes results where v5.050 was wrong.
findings.expected_measurement: Same results unless v5.050 miscompiled a design; a v5.050-only crash or mismatch would disappear.

findings.claim: The DFG fold of (a<<b)<<c into a<<(b+c) now computes b+c one bit wider, so an overflowing sum no longer wraps to a too-small shift amount.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Fix DFG nested shifts with overflowing shift amount (#7955) (#7977).' Commit a6f4dd03 message: "computed 'b + c' in the width of the shift-amount operand. When 'b + c' overflows that width it wraps around... Compute the sum one bit wider". v5.052 src/V3DfgPeephole.cpp:2551 REPLACE_SHIFTL_SHIFTL.
findings.impact: This only affects nested constant or dynamic shifts whose combined amount overflows, which is a v5.050 miscompile.
findings.expected_measurement: Identical results unless the design hit the bug.

findings.claim: Signed multiplies up to 64 bits in the runtime now multiply as unsigned to avoid C++ signed-overflow undefined behaviour. The bit result is unchanged on g++/x86.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Fix multiply undefined behavior on signed int overflow (#8247) (#8248).' v5.052 include/verilated_funcs.h:1198 `return static_cast<uint32_t>(lhs_signed) * static_cast<uint32_t>(rhs_signed);` (and the uint64_t form in VL_MULS_QQQ).
findings.impact: This only matters for SInt multiplies whose result is truncated. Values should be the same unless g++ previously exploited the undefined behaviour.
findings.expected_measurement: Identical DSL kernel results.

findings.claim: Generated models now run every scheduling region on each eval through runtime virtual calls, including empty regions. Upstream says this will hurt very small models.
findings.evidence: Commit 8546d5db (#8225): "the runtime eval loop calls everything unconditionally. If regions are empty, this is simply a call to an empty function. This will hurt performance on very small models". v5.052 include/verilated.cpp:4055-4135 VerilatedEvalLoop::evalImpl. Changes has no user-facing entry because the commit is marked Internals.
findings.impact: svsim calls eval() about twice per tick on small test DUTs. The overhead is likely negligible next to the DPI and pipe command cost.
findings.expected_measurement: Simulation wall time within noise of v5.050, possibly slightly slower for tiny DUTs.

findings.claim: DFG now synthesizes any combinational always block that drives exactly one variable, regardless of control-flow size, plus blocks that drive unused variables. This changes verilation time and the generated code for always_comb/case blocks.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Optimize more always blocks in DFG (#7775).' Commit 2285e5b6, src/V3DfgSynthesize.cpp: `-        if (!logicp->hasMultipleSinks() && cfg.nBlocks() <= 4 && cfg.nEdges() <= 4) {` becomes `+        if (!logicp->hasMultipleSinks()) worklist.push_front(*logicp);`. Related: '* Optimize circular logic in DFG (#7902)' makes V3DfgBreakCycles mandatory.
findings.impact: Firtool's always_comb/casez mux blocks are now in DFG's scope. This may change verilation time and runtime, and adds some miscompile risk.
findings.expected_measurement: Verilation and C++ build times may move by a few percent. Test results should be unchanged.

findings.claim: Building Verilator from source has the same requirements: configure.ac has no change to the C++ standard, bison, flex or python checks. The debug executable now defaults to -O0 -ggdb without -gz, and a new --enable-light-debug option restores -Og -ggdb1 -gz. configure also probes for -fsanitize=thread.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Add --enable-light-debug configure option (#7886).' configure.ac diff: `+  _MY_CXX_CHECK_OPT(CFG_CXXFLAGS_DBG,-O0)` / `-ggdb` in the default branch; `-gz` only `if test "$CFG_WITH_LIGHT_DEBUG" = "yes"`; `+_MY_CXX_CHECK_IFELSE(-fsanitize=thread, [AC_DEFINE([HAVE_TSAN]...`. docs/guide/install.rst is unchanged.
findings.impact: Ubuntu 24.04 with g++ 13 should build it as before. verilator_bin_dbg objects get larger because debug info is no longer compressed, but the -O0 dbg build compiles faster.
findings.expected_measurement: The source build succeeds with the same packages. Build directory size may grow and the dbg build time may change.

findings.claim: The v5.052 Changes file lists '* Fix NFA assertion scheduling to fix outcome counts (#7946).', but that change was reverted before the release. The entry is stale.
findings.evidence: Commit c81be029 'Fix NFA assertion scheduling to fix outcome counts (#7946)' was reverted by f694e9e1 'Revert NFA assertion outcomes (#7946 revert) (#8258)', which also removed the Changes line. Commit c4a4f35e 'Commentary: Changes update' re-added `+* Fix NFA assertion scheduling to fix outcome counts (#7946). [Yilou Wang]`. `git diff c81be029^ v5.052 -- src/V3AssertNfa.cpp src/V3Delayed.cpp` is empty, so the code is the pre-#7946 state.
findings.impact: Do not attribute any assertion-count change in v5.052 to #7946.
findings.expected_measurement: n/a

findings.claim: VerilatedContext and VerilatedScope destruction no longer depends on the thread-local current context, which fixes a segfault on context destruction.
findings.evidence: Changes: '* Fix segmentation fault on context destruction (#8265).' Commit e012f7c7, include/verilated.cpp: `~VerilatedContext() { Verilated::threadContextp(this); ... Verilated::threadContextp(nullptr); }` and `~VerilatedScope()` now uses `contextp()->impp()->scopeErase(this)` (m_symsp->_vm_contextp__) instead of Verilated::threadContextp().
findings.impact: svsim's teardown (`delete testbench; delete context;`, simulation-driver.cpp:1023-1024) destroys DPI VerilatedScopes. That path is now independent of the thread-local context, so it is safer at simulation exit.
findings.expected_measurement: No crashes at simulation exit (exit code 0 for passing tests).

research.notes:
I compared only git objects and ran no builds or simulations. There is no separate 5.051 release (tags: v5.050, v5.052). The only new Changes section is 'Verilator 5.052 2026-09-05', which is the former 5.051 devel. The diff had 314 commits.

The only unchanged areas: the thread pool, mutex, verilator_bin exit path, the jobs options and the $urandom RNG and seed handling all match v5.050. The thread-pool exit, jobs-option and RNG/seed results from the v5.050 run should carry over as they are.

The biggest structural change has no user-facing Changes entry because it is marked Internals: commit 8546d5db moved the eval loop into the runtime as VerilatedEvalLoop. The public model API and the init ordering are preserved, which matters for svsim's re-entrant eval from `always @(simulationState)`, so it should work unchanged. A rebuild of all 53 ChiselSim builds is the real confirmation.

The Changes entry for #7946 is stale: the code was reverted in f694e9e1 and the entry was re-added by c4a4f35e.

Low-confidence item: #8250 (V3Gate initial-statement fix, reported by a CIRCT developer). It could in principle touch firtool RANDOMIZE initial blocks, but I see no firtool pattern it would change. Checking whether results match v5.050 with RANDOMIZE_REG_INIT/MEM_INIT enabled would settle it.

Files consulted: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deterministic-vliw-chisel/72342c7d-9f6b-5534-9c62-327a6a17dee8/scratchpad/vsrc (git), /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deterministic-vliw-chisel/72342c7d-9f6b-5534-9c62-327a6a17dee8/scratchpad/svsim/simulation-driver.cpp, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deterministic-vliw-chisel/72342c7d-9f6b-5534-9c62-327a6a17dee8/scratchpad/svsim/svsim/Workspace.class (testbench template strings), and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deterministic-vliw-chisel/72342c7d-9f6b-5534-9c62-327a6a17dee8/scratchpad/verilated_5020.cpp for the 5.020 RNG seeding comparison.

verdicts.evidence: `git diff --quiet v5.050 v5.052 -- src/V3ThreadPool.cpp src/V3ThreadPool.h src/V3Mutex.h` returns rc=0. src/V3Global.cpp, src/V3Error.cpp and src/V3Os.h have no diff. V3Global.h only gains <type_traits> and the VRestorer* classes. V3Os.cpp only gains __wasi__ guards. The Verilator.cpp diff has these hunks: the V3Scoreboard.h include is removed, lowerSequenceEvents is added, evalp/evalNbap(nullptr) are dropped, and the selfTest list changes (adds AstClassRefDType::selfTest, drops VCMethod/V3ScoreboardBase/V3Order::selfTestParallel). At v5.052 Verilator.cpp:717 `V3MutexConfig...configure(verilateJobs()>1)`, :720 `threadPoolp(new V3ThreadPool{verilateJobs()})` and :926 `v3Global.shutdown()` are untouched. No thread-pool entry appears in the Changes diff. V3ThreadPool.cpp at v5.052: `V3ThreadPool(int numThreads){ numThreads=max(numThreads,1); if (numThreads==1) return; ...spawn workers }` and `enqueue()` runs `f()` inline when `m_workers.empty()`.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Nothing on the verilator_bin thread-pool or exit path changed between v5.050 and v5.052, so the 4931 exit race should behave as in v5.050. One detail in the impact text is imprecise. With `--verilate-jobs 1` V3ThreadPool is not a '1-thread pool': its constructor returns early, so it has no worker threads at all and enqueue() runs jobs inline on the main thread. Only `-j 0` (verilateJobs = nproc > 1) creates real worker threads, and that is the only setup where the exit race can occur. This explains the 0/3000 result for the two-option form. The expected_measurement (same abort rate as the v5.050 row, 0/3000 for the two-option form) is justified by code identity. Different verilation timing from the other changes may still shift the roughly 0.2% rate slightly.

verdicts.evidence: The v5.050..v5.052 diff of src/V3Options.cpp touches only the TSAN getSupported/showVersion code, `-assert-unroll-limit` (now CbVal that warns DEPRECATED) and `-fdfg-break-cycles`. At v5.052 `-build-jobs` (:1325, val==0 -> VlOs::getProcessDefaultParallelism()), `-verilate-jobs` (:1885) and the special `-j` parse (:~1999-2013, `-j 0` -> default parallelism) are unchanged. bin/verilator only gains the `+verilator+assert+lock` doc line. V3EmitMk.cpp: `putSet(var,value)` emits `VAR = value` (V3File.h:392), so it is cosmetic. The `make -j` comes from Verilator.cpp buildMakeCmd (:826-841), unchanged.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The claim is right, except for the expected_measurement wording. The `make -j <nproc>` for `--build-jobs 0` is added by `verilator --build` itself (Verilator.cpp buildMakeCmd: `-j N` if buildJobs>0 and MAKEFLAGS has no `-jobserver-auth`), not by the generated Makefiles. That code is unchanged.

verdicts.evidence: The v5.050..v5.052 diff of include/verilated.cpp has no hunk in the VlRNG/vl_thread_rng/vl_rng_state_from_seed block (v5.052 :425-548) or in randSeed()/randSeedDefault64() (:3693-3708). The seed parse in commandArgVl (:3621-3629) is also unchanged. verilated.h:528 has `m_randSeed = 1` (same at v5.050 :416), and verilated_imp.h:227 has `s_randSeedEpoch = 1`. In vl_thread_rng, `t_seedEpoch` starts at 0, so the first use always reseeds from randSeedDefault64() = (1<<32)^1. A bare run and `+verilator+seed+1` therefore give the same state. The scratchpad verilated_5020.cpp:349-362 shows 5.020 used `m_randSeed=0` (lrand48 default) and a direct state copy, so 5.020 differs. The scratchpad emulator rng546.py reproduces the measured 5.020 values ('old 1: fffffffc ff7fffff f77f7fff 8084023f', printed in reverse order). Its 'new' branch matches the v5.052 splitmix64/xoroshiro128** code line by line and predicts seed 1 (= no seed) as 5fa24450 24800459 fd8d9d77 b722072d in generation order. Commit 0e423a4b3 is first contained in tag v5.050 and c1e343d9c in v5.046 (git tag --contains), so both predate this range.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed. Clarification: `0e423a4b3` (seed default 1, 0 = random) first appears in v5.050, not v5.048. It is not part of the v5.050..v5.052 range. Prediction for v5.052: no seed == `+verilator+seed+1`, with the first 32-bit values 5fa24450 24800459 fd8d9d77 b722072d (the 5.020 measurement printed them in reverse order). Seed 2 gives 1be5aac4 516497e1 d3189547 fded6676. `+verilator+seed+0` is accepted and picks a random seed.

verdicts.evidence: Commit 1106e89c8 'Optimize random initialization' (message: fetch the thread-local once per variable; also remove unused VL_RAND_RESET_{Q,W}). Commit 8546d5db0 message: 'The model's eval and eval_step remain the top level entry points, and are backward compatible.' V3EmitCModel.cpp at v5.052 still emits `void eval(){ eval_step(); ...}` (:190), `eval_step()` (:195 and body :438-442 `m_evalLoop.eval()`), `final()`, `eventsPending()` (:214) and `nextTimeSlot()` (:216). VerilatedEvalLoop::evalImpl (verilated.cpp:4055) runs evalBegin, then `if(!m_didInit){evalStatic; evalInitial; settle loop; m_didInit=true}` (:4067-4078), then evalSample, ico, the nested loops, evalPostponed and evalEnd. v5.050 emitted `_eval_static; _eval_initial; _eval_settle; __Vm_didInit=true` (V3EmitCModel.cpp:418-423) and called `_sample` at the start of `_eval`. Commit 853ee5df1 adds DfgVertex::unsafe() (V3Dfg.cpp:483: true for DfgMux, and for DfgArraySel with a non-const index). It guards DfgLogAnd/LogOr/LogIf (`|| vtxp->rhsp()->unsafe()`) and the DfgCond rewrites (`&& !elsep->unsafe()` etc.). Test t_dfg_oob_array_access.v reads mem_reg[65535] of a 34001-element array under a guard. Note that dynamic bit selects (DfgMux) are always treated as unsafe, so these guard-dropping rewrites are now skipped for them. That can make generated code slightly less optimized for `cond && vec[idx]` patterns. This is a performance side effect, not a correctness one.

Commit e012f7c79: `~VerilatedContext()` now calls `Verilated::threadContextp(this)` at the start ('In unlikely case some other destructor needs it') and `Verilated::threadContextp(nullptr)` at the end. `VerilatedScope` ctor/dtor use the new `contextp()` (= m_symsp->_vm_contextp__) for scopeInsert/scopeErase instead of the thread-local context. The new test is t_wrapper_multicontext (several contexts in a vector). The svsim driver does `delete testbench; delete context;` (simulation-driver.cpp:1023-1024) with a single context.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Only VerilatedScope's constructor and destructor stop depending on the thread-local context; they now use their own context via m_symsp->_vm_contextp__. VerilatedContext's destructor does not stop depending on it. It temporarily sets the thread context to itself and clears it to nullptr at the end. The fix is for multi-context programs, where scope teardown used another context's thread-local. For svsim's single context it is neutral and harmless.

missed.claim: 'Fix heap-use-after-free in VlRNG::VlRNG() (#7865)' is in the Changes list but is not in the researcher's findings. The VlProcess destructor now resets the thread-local current process: `if (t_currentp == this) t_currentp = m_parentp.get();`. VlRNG was also made non-final and gained a VlRNGReseeds subclass (used by randomize()). The seeding algorithm and default seed are unchanged.
missed.evidence: Commit 58bd13b62, include/verilated_types.h:356. `VlProcess::currentRng()` returns `t_currentp->m_rng` if t_currentp is set, else the thread RNG (verilated.cpp:420-423). `VlProcess::currentp(...)` is only set from verilated_timing.cpp:39-44 and from generated vlProcess code (V3EmitCFunc.h:457-462).
missed.impact: The fix changes only the process-RNG fallback after a process dies. svsim builds without --timing/fork, so `$urandom` uses the thread RNG and the predicted seed-1/no-seed values are unaffected.

missed.claim: 'Fix dropping variable writes across opaque calls (#7921) (#7933)' is a V3Life lifetime-optimizer miscompile fix that the researcher did not list. In v5.050, a noopt condition (entry-point CCall such as DPI or public functions, timing, force, recursion) seen inside an if/else or loop body only cleared the nested block's map. The outer block's tracked variable values stayed valid, so writes could be dropped or forwarded stale. v5.052 propagates `m_noopt` to the block above in lifeToAbove().
missed.evidence: Commit 877fc1e81, src/V3Life.cpp: `bool m_noopt`, `noopt()`, `if (m_noopt) m_aboveLifep->noopt();`, and the loop/jumpblock bodies no longer call setNoopt. setNoopt callers at v5.052 V3Life.cpp:336, 351, 402, 421, 429, 439-440, 459. Test t_opt_life_loop_call.
missed.impact: This can only change results where a DPI or other entry-point call sits inside a branch or loop with variable writes around it. svsim's testbench has `if (simulationState==RUN) begin simulation_body(); simulationState=DONE; end`, but nothing is tracked outside that if, so a difference is unlikely. Firtool RTL has no such calls. It is still a v5.050 vs v5.052 miscompile difference to keep in mind.

missed.claim: 'Fix exponential expansion of nested selects (#8137) (#8151)' is not in the Changes file and is not in the findings. V3Expand's lowering of a narrow (<=64-bit) Sel from a wide source with a non-constant LSB was rewritten. If the derived word-index and shift expressions are larger than 8 nodes and the LSB expression is needed more than once, the LSB is evaluated into an `ExpandSel_Lsb` temporary.
missed.evidence: Commit 7523a0cd8, src/V3Expand.cpp (+195/-58), AstNode::isLargerThan() in V3Ast.h, test t_opt_expand_sel_wide_nested.
missed.impact: This is relevant to dynamic part-selects of >64-bit vectors (for example wide VLIW instruction bundles). It bounds verilation time and C++ size, but the generated C++ for such selects differs from v5.050 and slightly changes the verilation and compile time profile. Semantics are intended to be identical.
